title: Romulus Augustulus
summary: Romulus Augustulus (reigned 475–476 CE) was the last Western Roman emperor to rule in Italy. Raised to power as an adolescent on 31 October 475 by his father, the general Orestes, his regime lacked recognition from Constantinople. On or soon after 4 September 476, the Germanic general Odoacer killed Orestes, deposed Romulus, and spared him because of his youth, granting an annual pension and exiling him to Campania. His deposition is conventionally commemorated as marking the fall of the Western Roman Empire.

uncertainty.note: Birth date is estimated around 460–465. Death date is unknown; Mathisen records that he was still receiving his pension under Theodoric in 493 and again in 507 (or 511).

as_recorded.value: Then he entered Ravenna, deposed Augustulus from his throne, but in pity for his tender years, granted him his life; and being also moved by his beauty he gave him an annual allowance of six thousand solidi and sent him to Campania
on or soon after 4 September 476... In 493 and again in 507 (or 511), Romulus had to confirm his annual stipend with the new master of Italy, Theodoric

where.modern_name: Ravenna, Emilia-Romagna, Italy (seat of imperial court where Romulus was proclaimed and deposed)
where.historical_name: Ravenna, imperial residence of the Western Roman Empire

importance.justification: The deposition of Romulus Augustulus in September 476 removed the last western emperor recognized in Italy, providing the traditional chronological boundary for the end of the Western Roman Empire.

reviewer_note: Birth c. 460–465 CE is approximate. Deposition on or soon after 4 September 476 is documented in contemporary chronicles. Cassiodorus' Variae indicates Romulus was still receiving his 6,000-solidi pension in Campania in 507 or 511; his date of death remains unknown.
